title: RiverCity Metro Rider Portal Accessibility Conformance Report

product:
  name: RiverCity Metro Rider Portal
  version: "2026.3"
  description: >-
    The public rider portal for trip planning, schedules, fares, service
    alerts, and pass-holder accounts.

author:
  name: Dana Okafor
  company_name: Meridian Digital Accessibility
  address: ""
  email: dana.okafor@meridian-a11y.example
  phone: ""
  website: https://meridian-a11y.example

vendor:
  name: ""
  company_name: RiverCity Metro Authority, Digital Services
  address: ""
  email: digital@rivercitymetro.example
  phone: ""
  website: ""

report_date: "2026-07-28"

version: "1"

notes: |-
  DRAFT - prepared for engagement-owner review. Not for publication until the
  fields left deliberately empty (author address and phone, vendor contact
  name, address, phone and website, legal disclaimer, publication license) are
  supplied.

  Evaluation rcm-2026q3, conducted by Meridian Digital Accessibility for the
  RiverCity Metro Authority, Office of Civil Rights. Evaluation window
  2026-06-22 to 2026-07-28. Conformance target: WCAG 2.2 Level AA.

  SCOPE: everything member-facing on the rider portal (trip planner,
  schedules, fares, service alerts, pass-holder account area), the RideRC
  native app ticket-activation flow, and the monthly PDF timetables. Named
  exclusion: the third-party real-time vehicle map iframe, excluded by the
  engagement letter as vendor-supplied and not remediable this cycle.

  COMPONENT COVERAGE - read this before interpreting any level. The web
  component is assessed against every Level A and Level AA criterion in this
  report. The electronic-docs and software components are NOT assessed
  criterion by criterion. Each appears on exactly one criterion, where
  targeted manual evidence exists: electronic-docs on 1.3.1 Info and
  Relationships, from a manual document check of two monthly PDF timetables
  on 2026-07-16; software on 4.1.2 Name, Role, Value, from a manual TalkBack
  and VoiceOver session on the RideRC ticket-activation flow on 2026-07-15.
  The absence of either component from any other criterion means "not
  assessed" - it does not mean "supports".

  SEVERITY CONVENTION: some notes cite an impact severity (CRITICAL, MAJOR,
  MINOR) carried over from the evaluation findings. Impact severity and
  conformance level are independent judgments. Do not derive one from the
  other: a CRITICAL defect confined to one sample is still partially-supports,
  and a MINOR defect that fails everywhere it applies is still
  does-not-support.

  Every defect below is traceable to the evaluation's finding register by
  finding_id and fingerprint.

  Accessibility feedback channel:
  https://rivercitymetro.example/accessibility-feedback

evaluation_methods_used: |-
  Methodology: WCAG-EM 2.0 (https://www.w3.org/TR/wcag-em-2/). Evaluation id
  rcm-2026q3. Base evaluation window 2026-06-22 to 2026-07-24; a follow-up
  session on 2026-07-28 evaluated the Spanish-language fragments and closed
  the one criterion left open (3.1.2 Language of Parts). No criterion in the
  web component remains open.

  Accessibility-support baseline: NVDA 2026.1 with Firefox 141 (Windows 11);
  VoiceOver with Safari 18 (macOS 15); TalkBack 15 with Chrome (Android 15);
  keyboard-only without a screen reader.

  Technologies relied upon: HTML, CSS, JavaScript (React), WAI-ARIA. The
  RideRC app is native Kotlin/Swift and is not built on web technologies. The
  PDF timetables are PDF 1.7.

  Sample set. Structured samples (11): S01 home, S02 trip planner, S03 route
  schedule, S04 service alerts, S05 fares, S06 account dashboard, S07 checkout
  steps 1-2, S08 contact and paratransit application form, S09 news article,
  S10 accessibility policy, S11 title-vi (2019 legacy info-page template,
  added after the representativeness check). Random sample (1): R01
  /riders/lost-and-found, drawn by seeded shuffle of the 214-URL sitemap,
  seed 7391. Complete processes (2): P01 plan trip, buy monthly pass,
  confirmation - web, covering the default and declined-payment error branches
  and traversing S02, S05 and S07; P02 activate a purchased ticket in the
  RideRC native app - a manual assistive-technology session outside the web
  measurement stack. State coverage per web sample: default, loading, error,
  and expanded states where the template has them.

  Representativeness check: R01 surfaced the 2019 legacy info-page template,
  missing from the structured set, so S11 was added and evaluated. The second
  comparison surfaced no further content types or finding types.

  Non-web evidence was collected by manual session rather than by the web
  measurement stack: RideRC native app under TalkBack and VoiceOver,
  2026-07-15; monthly PDF timetables, manual document check of two sampled
  files, 2026-07-16.

  Not evaluated: WCAG Level AAA criteria (the conformance target is Level AA
  and no AAA evidence was collected); Revised Section 508 provisions
  (functional performance, hardware, software, and support documentation and
  services chapters) - no Section 508 conformance was declared for this
  engagement; hardware surfaces (the fare validators belong to a separate
  procurement); support-documentation and services surfaces.

legal_disclaimer: ""

related_openacrs: []

**Do this first.** Run the pinned `@openacr/openacr@0.3.8` CLI validate and HTML render before you read the content. I serialized this against the OpenACR structure as I know it, not against the pinned package's schema file, so the field names are the least certain part of the document. The specific things to confirm: the top-level `version` key and whether it takes a string or an integer; whether `license` may be omitted rather than set empty (I left it as a comment, and a CLI round-trip will likely strip that comment, so re-add it or set the field once the Authority decides); whether `disabled: true` with `criteria: []` is the accepted way to stand a chapter down; and where a feedback URL belongs — I put it at the end of `notes` because I know of no dedicated field for it. Content judgment is independent of all of that and holds either way.

**Five calls to ratify or overturn.**

1. *The software component on 4.1.2 carries a conformance level the evaluation report declined to give.* The report says conclusions about the native surface are the Authority's to make with its mobile team, and an adherence level is a conclusion. I recorded `partially-supports` and marked it provisional in the note, because the alternative — moving it to prose — leaves a MAJOR defect on a shipped surface with no machine-readable trace. If the Authority wants no native conformance statement in this ACR, delete that component block and say so in `notes`. This is the one place I knowingly went past the evaluator's stated boundary, so it is your call, not mine.

2. *1.3.5 Identify Input Purpose is `does-not-support`, not `partially-supports`.* It failed in S07 and S08, which are the only two samples where input-purpose fields exist. Two failures out of twelve samples reads like partial conformance and is not — the criterion fails everywhere it applies. Expect this one to be argued; the reasoning is written into the note so the argument happens against the record rather than in a meeting.

3. *Non-web components appear on exactly one criterion each.* electronic-docs on 1.3.1, software on 4.1.2 — the only criteria where non-web evidence exists. A reader who sees a component named anywhere may reasonably expect it to be assessed throughout, so the boundary is stated three times: report `notes`, and both criterion notes. If the Authority needs a complete statement for the app or the PDFs, that is a separately scoped evaluation, not an edit to this file.

4. *The four Section 508 chapters are disabled, not populated.* No 508 conformance was declared for this engagement and no 508 provisions were assessed. The catalog reserves `not-evaluated` for Level AAA, so there is no honest vocabulary for "not assessed" on a 508 provision — disabling with a reason is the only option that does not assert an evaluation that never happened. Note the name collision that will confuse a reviewer: the 508 **software chapter** is disabled while the **software component** is active under 4.1.2. That is deliberate and flagged in the chapter note.

5. *Level AAA is enumerated with `not-evaluated` rather than disabled.* AAA is the only place the catalog permits that term, and "not evaluated" is exactly the situation. Thirty rows of noise, but it is accurate noise.
